sermon.title: The Holy Spirit's Benefits and Ministry
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer teaches the benefits and ministry of the Holy Spirit: he gives life, testifies of Jesus, comforts, teaches, brings the word to remembrance, guides into all truth, shows practical things to come, and gives words before rulers. He contrasts “my faith” with the faith of Christ and applies these truths to work, family and civil leadership.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Two phrases not clear (26:40, 33:50). He cites James 2:17 for “show you my faith by my works” (2:18). Unchecked statistics: 400,000 cigarette deaths a year, 90,000 alcohol deaths, six million with alcohol disease, $240 billion alcohol medical costs (26:20–27:10); his claim that George W. Bush said the Bible is not a book of truth. Sensitive content kept as spoken: Obama, Osteen, Oprah, Bush, Bill Clinton, Romney/Joseph Smith, Ben Carson named; Islam; Catholicism; same-sex marriage; welfare; no pre-tribulation rapture.

chunks.section_question: What does “it is the Spirit who gives life” mean?

faqs.question: What two lives does the Bible speak of?
faqs.answer: The life that now is—family, home, job—and the life to come, eternal life with God.

faqs.question: Is the Bible a book of faith?
faqs.answer: He says it is a book of truth, and we must be established in truth.

faqs.question: Can we take credit for coming to God?
faqs.answer: No—he drew you and showed you your need.

faqs.question: Is it unspiritual to preach with notes?
faqs.answer: No—he says he needed notes as a young minister and there is nothing wrong with them.

faqs.question: Will the Spirit tell you something not in the Bible?
faqs.answer: No—if it isn’t backed by the Bible, it isn’t the Spirit.

faqs.question: Where should Christians get their perspective on news?
faqs.answer: From heaven—news from God brings it into proportion and balance.

faqs.question: Does the Holy Spirit tell you to sit on welfare?
faqs.answer: No—he will tell you to learn a job skill and work.

faqs.question: Is speaking in tongues proof of a changed life?
faqs.answer: No—without being driven to the Bible there is no change.

faqs.question: Should believers worry when arrested for their faith?
faqs.answer: No—God has a purpose and the Holy Spirit will give the words.
